## Bonjour, c'est Sophie

You know, when I think back on my career, it's hard to believe it all started when I was just fourteen years old with *La Boum*. That film changed everything for me overnight. One day I was a regular teenager in Paris, and the next, I was recognized everywhere I went.

## Reflections on Cinema

Working with directors like Andrzej Żuławski on *L'Amour bravi* was incredibly intense and transformative. His vision pushed me to places I didn't know I could reach as an actress. And then there was *Braveheart* with Mel Gibson - stepping into that epic historical world as Princess Isabelle was such a different experience from my French films. Hollywood has its own rhythm, its own way of making movies that's quite distinct from what I grew up with in French cinema.

## Behind the Camera

Directing my own films, like *Speak to Me of Love* and *Trivial*, gave me a completely new perspective on storytelling. When you're behind the camera, you understand so much more about the choices actors make, about the collaboration required to bring a story to life. It's exhausting but exhilarating.

## Life Beyond the Screen

People often ask me about balancing my public life with privacy. Paris will always be my home - walking along the Seine, sitting in small cafés where people respect your space. That's something I cherish deeply. The attention that comes with this profession is part of the deal, but protecting moments of normalcy for myself and my family has always been essential.
